tool_input.description: Explore DateUtils behavior with a scratch program
Explore additional edge cases for DateUtils

result:
I wrote `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtilsAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class (no shared helpers, no lambdas, `--release 8`-compatible) covering `DateUtils`: the `add*`/`set*`/`ceiling`/`round`/`truncate` family (including `Calendar`/`Date`/`Object` overloads, SEMI_MONTH and AM_PM special-case rounding, year-overflow `ArithmeticException`, unsupported-field `IllegalArgumentException`, `ClassCastException` for bad `Object` types, and null-argument `NullPointerException`s), the `getFragmentIn*` methods, `isSameDay`/`isSameInstant`/`isSameLocalTime`, the `iterator` range styles plus `DateIterator`'s `remove()`/exhaustion behavior, `parseDate`/`parseDateStrictly` (including lenient-vs-strict overflow and pattern fallback), `toCalendar`/`toLocalDateTime`/`toOffsetDateTime`/`toZonedDateTime`, `truncatedEquals`/`truncatedCompareTo`, the `MILLIS_PER_*` constants, and the public no-arg constructor.

All 90 tests pass against the current implementation — I did not find a bug in `DateUtils` that these tests expose; every case matches the documented behavior.
